statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit of five representative page archetypes plus an HTTP failure state. Account/payment/auth routes were not covered because they are not exposed in the public journey; those contextual checks are explicitly N/A.

page.notes: Public adult video catalogue behind an AgeGo verification overlay. Content is substantially server-rendered. The repository web-uplift.json describes only the local playground and was not applied to this unrelated remote site.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot or computed background under an emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark condition will reveal whether surfaces re-tint; the page CSS / a color-scheme declaration is corroborating evidence. The model chooses the method.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-condition capture retains the same fixed dark age panel and blurred light page treatment; the probe reports `color-scheme: normal` and no site colour-scheme adaptation.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video, or an in-page probe of getAnimations()/computed animation under an emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce condition, can show whether motion stops. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `document.getAnimations()` returned an empty list; no auto-advance motion was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot under emulated prefers-contrast: more / forced-colors, or an axe/contrast probe, can show whether controls and text survive. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under `prefers-contrast: more`, the probe reports the focused button outline as `none`; Lighthouse also identifies multiple 2.35–3.16:1 text contrast failures.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video of a route/state change shows whether it animates; the page source / ::view-transition usage corroborates. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The UI probe found no `document.startViewTransition` use; navigation is a conventional multi-page anchor flow and custom overlays swap state without a transition.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and applicability judgement across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: No scroll-linked animation or scrollytelling surface exists on the representative templates, so there is no scroll animation implementation to assess.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked animation or scrollytelling surface exists on the representative templates, so there is no scroll animation implementation to assess.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative pages use native scrolling and links; no custom pointer-driven gesture layer or scroll-snap override was found.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video of scrolling, or CSS inspection for scroll-state container queries. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile layout is 22,604px tall while the UI probe found zero sticky elements; no progress, shrinking header, or position-aware chrome was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for anchor-name / position-anchor / position-try on overlays; a screenshot of an open overlay near a viewport edge can show drift. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The rendered DOM has a custom `.lang_trigger` and four custom fixed layers, but zero popovers/dialogs; the gate and banners are manually layered at high z-index.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for ::highlight / scroll-marker; a transition video can show whether attention is cued after navigation. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Visible global navigation, current-page headings and descriptive taxonomy links provide clear destination cues across covered templates.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot on load, or a DOM probe for full-viewport overlays present before interaction. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The first viewport is entirely occupied by the age overlay; DOM/network evidence also shows `popunder1000.js`, multiple ad-provider scripts, a cookie banner and fixed ad layers.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/source inspection for popover / <dialog> / <details> vs custom overlay divs with manual dismiss handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The UI probe found 0 dialogs, 0 popovers and 0 details while the DOM contains custom `age-popup`, `cookiesBanner`, ad layers and `agego-overlay-container`.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot plus layout metrics can show the proportion of the viewport given to chrome vs content. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Recon found multiple ad iframes and fixed ad layers; the HAR records 116 third-party requests across 15 origins before the user reaches content.

checkOutcomes.method: layout metrics (scrollWidth vs innerWidth) and a screenshot at an emulated narrow mobile viewport reveal overflow. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: At 360x800, layout reports scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 and horizontalOverflowPx=0 with a viewport meta tag.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for @container / container-type; a computed-style probe of the same component in a wide vs narrow container shows whether it adapts. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The UI probe found zero elements with a non-normal `container-type`; sampled tags/list/video components also report `container-type: normal`.

checkOutcomes.method: a focus probe (focus an element, read the computed outline) or an axe target-size check; a screenshot of a focused control corroborates. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The focus probe found the cookie OK and search submit buttons with `outline: none`; many metadata links are only 18–20px high.

paths.description: Homepage/listing archetype and age-verification entry; represents video grids and primary browse journey.
Popular listing archetype; selected to represent alternate ranked video grids.
Taxonomy/index archetype; selected for dense navigation and mobile adaptation.
Video detail and playback archetype; selected as the primary content-consumption journey.
Long-form policy/content archetype; selected for trust, legibility and data-practice context.
Invalid-route recovery state; selected to test HTTP and user recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition capture retains the same fixed dark age panel and blurred light page treatment; the probe reports `color-scheme: normal` and no site colour-scheme adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme: light dark` and define preference-driven surface/text tokens with `prefers-color-scheme` or `light-dark()`.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences do not preserve visible focus and sufficient contrast.
findings.evidence: Under `prefers-contrast: more`, the probe reports the focused button outline as `none`; Lighthouse also identifies multiple 2.35–3.16:1 text contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a `prefers-contrast: more` treatment, retain system/forced colours, and provide a strong `:focus-visible` indicator.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The UI probe found no `document.startViewTransition` use; navigation is a conventional multi-page anchor flow and custom overlays swap state without a transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route/state continuity, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Very long listings provide no scroll-state-aware navigation aid.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout is 22,604px tall while the UI probe found zero sticky elements; no progress, shrinking header, or position-aware chrome was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight sticky/scroll-state-aware navigation or progress affordances on long listing and policy pages.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays use custom positioning rather than semantic anchored primitives.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM has a custom `.lang_trigger` and four custom fixed layers, but zero popovers/dialogs; the gate and banners are manually layered at high z-index.
findings.suggestedFix: Use Popover and CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions for transient menus; use dialog only for true modal flows.

findings.summary: Popunder/ad code and stacked full-screen UI interrupt content before the user can browse.
findings.evidence: The first viewport is entirely occupied by the age overlay; DOM/network evidence also shows `popunder1000.js`, multiple ad-provider scripts, a cookie banner and fixed ad layers.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the required age gate, but remove popunders, defer non-essential ads until after consent, and avoid stacking banners over it.

findings.summary: Dismissible UI is built from custom fixed divs rather than platform primitives.
findings.evidence: The UI probe found 0 dialogs, 0 popovers and 0 details while the DOM contains custom `age-popup`, `cookiesBanner`, ad layers and `agego-overlay-container`.
findings.suggestedFix: Rebuild transient banners with Popover/light-dismiss and modal flows with `<dialog>` plus explicit focus management.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome competes heavily with the core video content.
findings.evidence: Recon found multiple ad iframes and fixed ad layers; the HAR records 116 third-party requests across 15 origins before the user reaches content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove low-value ad placements and consolidate the header so content and search dominate each viewport.

findings.summary: Components rely on page-level sizing rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The UI probe found zero elements with a non-normal `container-type`; sampled tags/list/video components also report `container-type: normal`.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards, taxonomy blocks and player metadata where components appear at different widths.

findings.summary: Some controls lack visible keyboard focus and many link targets are too short.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found the cookie OK and search submit buttons with `outline: none`; many metadata links are only 18–20px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clear `:focus-visible` ring and enlarge/pad compact links and icon controls to robust touch target sizes.

findings.summary: The 404 state has no recovery route or useful next action.
findings.evidence: The invalid-route probe returns only “Not Found / The requested URL was not found on this server” and exposes zero links.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 with search, home/popular links, and a clear recovery message while preserving the 404 status.

findings.summary: Load performance misses the good Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.7s, TBT 390ms and performance 0.55; the independent trace measured LCP 3.36s and 196ms blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, defer third-party scripts, and reduce render-blocking dependencies.

findings.summary: Third-party and legacy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded a 240ms long task and 196ms TBT; Lighthouse reported 3.4s of main-thread work and 390ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove non-essential third-party JavaScript and split/defer remaining work away from startup.

findings.summary: Resource delivery has long blocking chains and weak cache/image delivery.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1.82s savings from render-blocking requests; HAR identifies parser-inserted synchronous scripts, and Lighthouse flags cache/font/image delivery opportunities.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer parser-blocking scripts, set durable cache headers, preload only critical assets, and use `font-display` plus responsive image delivery.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 874KiB of unused JavaScript and 53KiB of legacy JavaScript; the HAR loads 18 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete duplicate/unused bundles, conditionally load features and ads, and serve a modern bundle.

findings.summary: Search, images, links and third-party frames have missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image-alt, link-name and frame-title; the direct probe finds an unlabelled search input and untitled iframes.
findings.suggestedFix: Label search, name icon links/buttons, add meaningful alt text, and title or hide decorative iframes.

findings.summary: Text and essential controls fail WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports repeated 2.35–2.45:1 blue-on-white failures and a 3.16:1 age-verification label.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken accent colours or adjust backgrounds to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and validate all interaction states.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and document structure are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Direct focus testing found buttons with no outline; the video detail has no H1, while its player is the primary content surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide visible `:focus-visible` styles, one descriptive H1 per detail page, landmarks, and a logical focus order.

findings.summary: Compact targets and captionless video reduce inclusive access.
findings.evidence: The direct probe lists many 18–20px-high targets; the representative video has zero `<track>` captions. The viewport allows scaling, but those failures remain.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target hit areas and provide captions/transcripts for video, keeping user scaling enabled.

findings.summary: Several assets are unsized or displayed at the wrong aspect ratio.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image aspect ratio and partially fails unsized images; the images primitive finds 2 missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or `aspect-ratio` and generate correctly cropped responsive derivatives.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and DevTools inspector issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecated-API warning and fails the Inspector Issues audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use, resolve DevTools Issues, and verify BFCache/source-map health in a clean profile.

findings.summary: The sitemap endpoint is empty despite a large public catalogue.
findings.evidence: Canonical URLs, 200 status and robots.txt are present, but `/sitemap.xml` returns HTTP 200 with Content-Length 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish segmented XML sitemaps for videos, tags and models and reference them from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Core security headers are missing and cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; all four observed cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP, HSTS and nosniff, and set Secure plus the narrowest viable SameSite policy on every cookie.

findings.summary: The pre-consent third-party and tracking footprint is excessive.
findings.evidence: The load contacts 15 third-party origins with 116 requests; known Google trackers and numerous ad origins run before content access.
findings.suggestedFix: Block analytics/ads until informed consent, remove popunder/session-wide tracking, and minimise/batch remaining telemetry.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced privacy and isolation policies are largely absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP or nosniff; only X-Frame-Options is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP `frame-ancestors`, and consider Trusted Types for script-heavy surfaces.

findings.summary: The startup experience depends on fragile custom overlays and third-party frames.
findings.evidence: Recon shows four high-z-index custom fixed layers and untitled ad frames; several captures show the gate panel before its content finishes, leaving an opaque blocking surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce startup overlays, use platform top-layer primitives, add deterministic loading/error states, and isolate third-party failures.

findings.summary: HTTP failure states are unbranded and unrecoverable.
findings.evidence: The tested 404 has no navigation, search, retry or home link, only the server’s generic error text.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide intentional 404/network failure states with recovery controls and preserve user context.

findings.summary: Popunder advertising and pre-consent tracking undermine predictable, honest interaction.
findings.evidence: Loaded source includes `popunder1000.js` and multiple ad-provider scripts; 116 third-party requests occur while the age wall blocks the core content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove popunders, clearly label external promotions, and require explicit consent before non-essential tracking.

findings.summary: Images are not delivered responsively or in efficient formats.
findings.evidence: The images audit finds 98/100 without srcset, 9 oversized and 10 legacy-format images; Lighthouse estimates 441KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive derivatives, use `srcset`/`sizes`, and right-size each card image.

findings.summary: The page performs disproportionate background/ad work before core content.
findings.evidence: HAR records 124 requests and 1.39MB in this capture, including 62 fetch/XHR calls; Lighthouse separately observes a 4.6MiB load and 874KiB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate chatty ad/analytics requests, batch telemetry, and conditionally load code only when used.

findings.summary: Third parties dominate the request and byte budget.
findings.evidence: 116 of 124 HAR requests and 1.30MB of 1.39MB transferred are classified third-party; GTM alone transfers 161KB and 15 third-party origins run.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget, remove low-value networks, self-host essential assets, and defer media/ads until user intent.

Replace custom overlays with resilient semantic top-layer UI
